item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a 2024 source showing a broad Srettha-era equality agenda for women, indigenous groups, or regional minorities beyond the marriage-equality case and the Tak Bai accountability issue. The strongest positive evidence is specific to LGBT equality; the negative evidence is broader and hits minorities, dissidents, and marginalized border-region communities more directly.","evidence":[{"title":"Thailand: Promptly Pass Same-Sex Marriage Bill","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"March 27, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/27/thailand-promptly-pass-same-sex-marriage-bill","summary":"Thailand’s House passed the Marriage Equality Act by an overwhelming margin under Srettha’s government. This is direct evidence that the government supported legal equality for LGBT people, a major excluded group.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Victory for Same-Sex Marriage in Thailand","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"June 18, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/victory-same-sex-marriage-thailand","summary":"Thailand’s Senate approved the same-sex marriage bill, making Thailand the first country in Southeast Asia to recognize same-sex relationships. This is the strongest 2024 evidence that Srettha’s government supported equal civil status for an excluded group.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Thailand","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024 report page","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/thailand","summary":"HRW notes that marriage equality had already been approved in principle and was moving through the system in 2024, even while broader rights enforcement remained weak. This is supportive background for LGBT equality, but it is narrower than a broad equality program.","question_ids":["4B.7"]},{"title":"Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"May 1, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice","summary":"HRW says successive Thai governments failed to prosecute officials responsible for deaths and injuries of ethnic Malay Muslim protesters in Tak Bai, and urges Srettha to end the impunity. This is strong negative evidence for political equality for a minority and an opposition region.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"January 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights","summary":"HRW says the new government had not seriously reformed rights protections and should end politically motivated prosecutions of peaceful protesters and monarchy critics. This indicates continuing inequality in treatment of unpopular viewpoints.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Thailand: Swap-Mart Targets Foreign Dissidents and Refugees","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"May 15, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/15/thailand-swap-mart-targets-foreign-dissidents-refugees","summary":"HRW says Thai authorities cooperated in transnational repression against dissidents and refugees, including harassment, surveillance, and deportation without due process. That is direct evidence against equal protection for excluded and unpopular groups.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5"]},{"title":"Thailand: Investigate Detained Youth Activist’s Death","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"May 23, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/23/thailand-investigate-detained-youth-activists-death","summary":"HRW says hundreds of monarchy critics were in pretrial detention and calls for a transparent investigation into a custodial death. This supports the view that unpopular viewpoints still faced selective coercion rather than equal political standing.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.3","4B.5"]},{"title":"Thailand | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"June 17, 2024","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand","summary":"The report says Thai media remained free to criticize government policy and cover corruption, but also says journalists self-censored around the military, judiciary, and lèse-majesté. This is mixed evidence, but the self-censorship side weighs against broad protection of unpopular viewpoints.","question_ids":["4B.7","4B.3","4B.6","4B.5"]}]}
